_comment: Single source of truth. Every row is a real repo verified live on 2026-10-07 via the GitHub API through the charetterat HK proxy. Stars are a snapshot, not a constant. 'why_here' explains what a reader gets. Nothing is inferred — anything we did not verify live is marked so.
_scope: Running one LLM across MORE THAN ONE device you already own — phones, Macs, PCs, boards, browsers — instead of buying a bigger GPU. Cross-device pooled/split/p2p inference. NOT model-parallel research frameworks, NOT cloud API gateways, NOT single-device VRAM tricks (those get one section each, clearly bounded).

entries.name: Backburner
entries.hardware: M-series Mac + iPhone 15 Pro or newer over USB-C
entries.what: Your iPhone runs the tail layers (prefill) or old-KV attention (decode) while the Mac runs the rest, pipelined over a 10 Gb/s cable. Measured +29-44% prefill at 16k-48k ctx, 196k-229k context at 8-bit on an iPhone 17 Pro Max. Greedy output token-identical with and without the phone.
entries.requirements: Apple Silicon Mac (tested M4 Pro 24 GB); iPhone 15 Pro+; a 10 Gb/s USB-C cable (the cable in the iPhone box is USB 2 and too slow); AltStore for the app; sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb reset after every reboot
entries.why_here: The entry that made this list necessary. Ships bench/*.jsonl raw data and names what it did NOT test. 78 forks in 6 days; community results threads are open.
gotchas: 8 GB Macs: stock 27B does not fit — split decode is the path (docs/SPLIT-DECODE.md), ~4 tok/s on a MacBook Neo + iPhone Air
iPhone Air's port is USB 2 (480 Mb/s) — the cable bottleneck is real per-device, check your port before blaming the software
macOS resets the GPU wired-memory limit on every reboot; re-run the sysctl or the model gets paged out
entries.summary: iPhone helps a Mac run a bigger model over one cable

entries.name: Pooled
entries.what: Peer-to-peer LLM inference in the browser: pool your devices over WebRTC to run big open models, for chat and coding agents. No install — it runs in a tab.
entries.why_here: Same 'devices you already own' idea as Backburner but with zero cable and zero install; the devices talk WebRTC. Good when your second device is a phone you don't want to jailbreak-side-load.
entries.summary: P2P inference in the browser — every device with a tab joins the pool

entries.name: exo
entries.hardware: Macs, GPUs, phones on one network
entries.what: Run frontier models distributed across your existing devices. The incumbent in this space — if you have several Apple-silicon machines this is the lowest-friction path.
entries.why_here: The benchmark every project in this list is implicitly compared against. Included so you don't have to discover it from a benchmark table.
entries.summary: The incumbent: frontier models across your existing devices

entries.name: lmstudio-two-pc-split
entries.hardware: two PCs on one LAN (AMD Radeon + anything, Vulkan)
entries.what: Run a model too big for one GPU in LM Studio across two PCs over LAN, via llama.cpp RPC: two DLLs + one env var (GGML_RPC_SERVERS). No LM Studio source changes.
entries.why_here: The cheapest possible demo of llama.cpp RPC splitting: if you thought you needed a framework, this shows two DLLs and an env var can be the whole thing.
entries.summary: Two PCs, one model, LM Studio: two DLLs + one env var

entries.name: DRIFT
entries.what: One LLM split across a Mac and a Windows PC — heterogeneous pipeline inference over a framework-neutral wire, bit-for-bit identical to single-machine. No torch.distributed.
entries.why_here: The only entry here that spans Apple + NVIDIA in one pipeline with an output-equivalence claim.
entries.summary: One model split across a Mac (MPS) + Windows PC (CUDA)

entries.name: llamacpp-distributed-inference
entries.what: A GUI wrapper that turns llama.cpp RPC into a point-and-click distributed setup across machines on a local network.
entries.why_here: If the two-DLL route is too manual, this is the GUI alternative for the same underlying llama.cpp RPC mechanism.
entries.summary: GUI wrapper for llama.cpp RPC across a LAN

entries.name: esp32s3-distributed-ai
entries.what: Distributed 56M-parameter LLM inference across three ESP32-S3 boards, split-PLE + KV cache, fully offline, no OS.
entries.why_here: The extreme small end. Proof the split principle works on boards with no OS and megabytes of RAM — a useful boundary marker for what 'pooling' can mean.
entries.summary: One LLM across 3 ESP32 boards, fully offline

entries.name: network-container
entries.what: Distributed LLM cluster pooling RAM/VRAM across machines, with no central 51% orchestrator and workers free to leave.
entries.why_here: Interesting governance take on pooling (workers own their compute). Early — zero stars — listed because the mechanism differs from everything else here.
gotchas: no license file — check before redistributing any part of it
entries.summary: RAM/VRAM pool across machines, no central orchestrator

entries.name: tensorgrid
entries.what: Distributed unified compute runtime in Rust — pools CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM across computers on a local network.
entries.why_here: Same goal as exo but written in Rust and aimed at heterogeneous LANs rather than a Mac-first experience. Early.
entries.summary: Rust runtime pooling CPU/RAM/GPU across a LAN

entries.name: memcloud
entries.what: Distributed in-memory data store in Rust — nodes pool RAM into a shared KV store aimed at LLM serving, mDNS discovery, peer-to-peer.
entries.why_here: Not inference itself: it is the memory tier that a split inference setup can sit on. Listed for that specific role.
entries.summary: Pooled RAM as a KV-store memory tier (dormant)

entries.name: OpenFabric
entries.what: Zero-config decentralized local compute mesh: pool RAM, GPU VRAM and storage across machines to run distributed AI models and sandboxed workloads.
entries.why_here: The widest hardware envelope here (Raspberry Pi included). Very early.
entries.summary: Zero-config mesh incl. Raspberry Pi (very early)

entries.name: moe-l2
entries.what: MoE expert offload for low-VRAM GPUs — run 100B+ MoE models on 8 GB cards via expert caching with LRU hot experts, OpenAI-compatible proxy, GGUF.
entries.why_here: Listed as the boundary of this list: it is the strongest single-device alternative when your second device isn't available. If you can't pool, this is what to compare against.
entries.summary: Single-device alternative: 100B+ MoE on an 8 GB card

entries.name: dsv41-flash-offload
entries.what: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash EXL3 on one 24 GB card with staged-DMA prefill, CPU expert tier, elastic VRAM expert cache, weights on disk, OpenAI API.
entries.why_here: The other boundary entry: RAM+SSD as the 'second device' on one box. Compare pooled-vs-tiered on your own workload before choosing.
gotchas: single machine; the 'pooling' is across memory tiers, not devices
entries.summary: Single-device alternative: RAM+SSD tiering on one 3090

entries.name: ComfyUI-MultiGPU
entries.what: One-click 'Virtual VRAM' for ComfyUI UNet/CLIP loaders plus MultiGPU integration, managing offload and block swap.
entries.why_here: Image generation, not LLM — listed because it is the mature proof that block-swap offload works at scale, and image-gen readers outnumber LLM readers for this technique.
gotchas: ComfyUI/workflow only; not a chat or agent runtime
entries.summary: Image-gen sibling: mature block-swap proof (not LLM)
